{{nihongo|'''Kasami Shrine'''|加佐美神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

'''Kasami Shrine'' (Kasami Shrine) is {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}{{ill|Kakamigahara|Q641491|qid=Q641491}}{{ill|Sohara Old Market Town|Q131870109|qid=Q131870109}}. Located on the left bank of {{ill|Shinsakai River|Q11501642|qid=Q11501642}}, east-southeast of Mt. Kasami.{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchisha}}. Originally 10 villages of Sohara ({{ill|Ibijima|Q18990514|qid=Q18990514|lt=Ibuki, Asuka, Shimazaki}}, {{ill|Wagō|Q23940976|qid=Q23940976|lt=Noguchi, Kumada, Higashijima, Sakai}}, {{ill|Ōmiya|Q18748127|qid=Q18748127|lt=Oshima/Miyashiro}}・{{ill|Furuichiba|Q22125133|qid=Q22125133|lt=Furuichi Market}}) is {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}}, but it is currently considered to be the Sojajin of {{ill|Sohara|Q11625179|qid=Q11625179|lt=Sohara District}} and {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}}. {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old company rank}} is a Gosha.

It is one of the {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592}} five shrines in Kakamigahara City, <ref>[https://www.tezikarao.org/news/detail.php?id=149 Kakamigahara City Kinpei Five Shrines Tour], Gifu Prefectural Shrine Agency Kakamigahara City Branch</ref>.

=== Summary ==={{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}} ({{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jokan}}6), founded by {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243}}. In the past, this area was ruled by {{ill|Soga clan|Q909854|qid=Q909854}} such as {{ill|Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawa no Maro|Q3488899|qid=Q3488899}}, and the place name ``Sohara'' is said to have come from the Soga clan's possession. It is said that after Sogakura Yamada Ishikawamaro passed away, the people of Sohara Manor (currently Sohara) worshiped him and held rituals there, and the shrine itself may have existed in the {{ill|7th century|af|7de eeu|als|7. It is said that around {{ill|905|Q24239|qid=Q24239}} ({{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}}5), it was located in {{ill|Kakami district|Q11412369|qid=Q11412369}} Soharasho Old Market and was called Hachiman Shrine. It is said that it was called Kasami Myojin in {{ill|908|Q30463|qid=Q30463}} (Engi 8). Furthermore, according to the middle volume of "{{ill|Fuken Gōsha Meiji Jinja Shiryō|Q11486103|qid=Q11486103|lt=Fugata Gosha Meiji Shrine Journals}}" published {{ill|1912|Q2077|qid=Q2077}} (Meiji 45), the {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} and the year of its founding are unknown<ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=Gifu Prefecture |journal={{ill|Fuken Gōsha Meiji Jinja Shiryō|Q11486103|qid=Q11486103|lt=Prefectural Gosha Meiji Shrine Magazine}} |volume=Volume 2 |publisher=Meiji Shrine Magazine |date=1912-01-15 |pages=36-37 |doi=10.11501/1088278}}</ref>.In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, there is "Kasami Shrine" in the seven temples of Kagami District in {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156|lt=Minokuni}} Kaminashita |journal={{ill|Kokushi Taikei|Q10926780|qid=Q10926780|lt=Kokushi Taikei}} |volume=13 |publisher={{ill|Keizai Zasshisha|Q11606486|qid=Q11606486}} |date=1900-11-15 |pages=346 |doi=10.11501/991103}}</ref>, "Minokuni Shinmecho" lists "{{ill|Senior Fourth Rank|Q11123338|qid=Q11123338|lt=Senior Fourth Rank Lower}}Kasamita Myojin" among the 23 shrines in Kagami-gunza<ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |editor={{ill|Saeki Ariyoshi|Q11382847|qid=Q11382847}} etc. |title=Enryakuji Hon Mino Province Shinmecho |journal=Jingi Zensho |volume=Volume 4 |publisher={{ill|Koten Kokyusho|Q11580997|qid=Q11580997}} |date=1908-05-17 |pages=624 |doi=10.11501/991328}}</ref><ref name="Kakamigahara City History">{{Cite journal |Japanese book |editor=Kakamigahara City Board of Education |title=Section 2 Shrines as seen in the Engishiki Shinmyocho |journal=Kakamigahara City History |volume=General history Nature, primitive, ancient, medieval |publisher=Kakamigahara City |date=1986-12-20 |pages=626-630 |doi=10.11501/9571788}}</ref>. In addition, in the "Kakamigahara City History", "{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}" August 15, 864 {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kimi}}Article ``{{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}{{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|ko|종5위|zh|從五位|qid=Q11071125|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower}}Kasami Kamishō<small>ku </small><sub>Two</sub>Junior Fifth Rank Upper<small>wo</small><sub>One</sub>'', but at the time of {{Efn|{{ill|Quotation|Q206287|qid=Q206287}}, {{ill|Chinese numerals|Q683566|qid=Q683566}} was changed to {{ill|Arabic numerals|Q29961325|qid=Q29961325}}. }}<ref name="Kakamigahara City History"/>, the description varies depending on the manuscript. In the past, there were two torii gates and three torii gates on the approach to the shrine, and the latter gate was connected to Sowara Chuo Dori and {{ill|Kakamigahara|Q641491|qid=Q641491|lt=Ogase Kaido}}. The intersection, Sannotorii, is said to have existed at the intersection of Sowara Chuo-dori Street and {{ill|Kakamigahara|Q641491|qid=Q641491|lt=Yamada-dera Street}}<ref name="Key Scenic Area">{{Cite book |Japanese book |url=https://www.city.kakamigahara.lg.jp/_res/projects/default_project/_page_/001/008/305/03_kasami240815.pdf |title=Kakamigahara City District Landscape Plan Landscape Formation Standards Guidelines Key Scenic District 3 Kasami Shrine District |format=PDF |publisher=Kakamigahara City |page=1 |accessdate=2025-02-26}}</ref>.Kasami Shrine once had Ichinomiya, Ninomiya, and Sannomiya, and Ichinomiya was the Shinmei Shrine in Furuichiba Village, Kagami District (now Sohara Furuichiba Town). (Kakamigahara City, Sohara Furuichiba Town)|Q134987025|Shinmei Shrine}}, Ninomiya is {{jalink|Yasaka Shrine} in Ibuki Village, Kakamiga District (currently {{ill|Sohara Ibuki Town|ja|蘇原伊吹町|qid=Q131900799}}) (Sohara Ibuki-cho, Kakamigahara City)|Q134928112|Yasaka Shrine}}, Sannomiya is Kumano Shrine {{Efn|{{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} (Meiji 42), {{ill|Shinmei Shrine (Noguchi-chō, Sohara, Kakamigahara)|ja|神明神社 (各務原市蘇原野口町)|qid=Q134926762|lt=Shinmei Shrine}} ({{ill|Sohara Noguchi Town|ja|蘇原野口町|qid=Q131870111}}). }}<ref name="base stone">From the local commentary board ``Kasami Shrine "Nino Torii" base stone''</ref>. == Enshrined God ==
* Kasami Okami
** According to one theory, ``Kasamiyama'' itself, located to the west-northwest of Kasami Shrine, was once an object of worship. It is assumed that Kasami Okami considered Mt. Kasami as a god.

== Main rituals ==
Based on "Shikiuchi Kinpeisha Kasami Shrine Bookmark".
* January 1st - {{ill|Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824}}, Good Luck Prayer Festival, Traffic Safety Festival
* February Setsubun - {{ill|Setsubun|Q746798|qid=Q746798}} Festival
* February 14th of the lunar calendar - Akiba Festival
* February 20th - {{ill|Kinensai|Q118906710|qid=Q118906710}}・Okuwa Festival
* March 15th - Sumiyoshi Festival
* First Saturday of April - Okunomiya Festival/Suijin Festival
* Last Sunday of July - {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|Q11261910|qid=Q11261910}} Shinto ritual
* Second Sunday before October 15th - {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469|lt=Reitaisai}}
** It used to be held on October 14th and 15th every year. A flower mikoshi is carried out. Previously, the Kenka Mikoshi was dedicated, but it was temporarily suspended due to an accident, but the "Rokken Mikoshi Association" centered around {{ill|Sohara Rokkencho|Q131900816|qid=Q131900816}} has revived the Kenka Mikoshi as a mock performance.<ref>{{Cite web |Japanese book |url=https://rokken-mikoshi.jimdosite.com/ |title=Rokuken Mikoshi Association |accessdate=2025-05-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |Japanese book |url=https://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/791540 |title=Vertically ``Fighting Mikoshi'' Regular festival at Kakamigahara Kasami Shrine |newspaper={{ill|Chunichi Shimbun|Q904678|qid=Q904678}} |date=2023-10-19}}</ref>.* November 15th - {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|Q1072387|qid=Q1072387}} Festival
* November 23rd - New Grain Thanksgiving
* December 31st - {{ill|Chinese New Year's Eve|Q7245702|qid=Q7245702}} Festival
* 1st and 15th of every month - Monthly Festival

== Cultural assets ==
* Wooden guardian dog
** A wooden {{ill|Komainu|Q20155846|qid=Q20155846}} approximately 115cm tall. It is thought to have been produced in the early {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} period. City-designated cultural property ({{ill|1974|Q2478|qid=Q2478}} (June 26, 1974)) <ref name="City-designated cultural property">{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.kakamigahara.lg.jp/kankobunka/bunkazai/1005178.html |title=City-designated cultural property |access-date=2025-03-04 |publisher=Kakamigahara City}}</ref><ref name="Kasami Shrine"/><ref name="Wooden guardian dog">{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.kakamigahara.lg.jp/kankobunka/bunkazai/1011515/1005217.html |title=Is there actually only one “guardian dog”? Elegant wooden sculpture |access-date=2025-03-04 |publisher=Kakamigahara City}}</ref>.
* Kasami Shrine Lion Head** A wooden lion head donated by Noguchi Village, Kagami District in {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}}3 ({{ill|1675|Q7624|qid=Q7624}}). During the annual shrine festival procession in October, a lion head leads the mikoshi procession. City-designated cultural property ({{ill|1970|Q2474|qid=Q2474}} (March 23, 1974)) <ref name="City-designated cultural property"/><ref name="Kasami Shrine"/><ref name="Lion Head">{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.kakamigahara.lg.jp/kankobunka/bunkazai/1011515/1005225.html |title=A regional treasure where the legend of "Oshishi-sama" is passed down |access-date=2025-03-04 |publisher=Kakamigahara City}}</ref>.

== Transportation ==
* {{ill|Gifu Bus|Q5560101|qid=Q5560101|lt=Gifu Bus}} Get off at Ozaki Danchi Line "Sohara" {{ill|Bus stop|Q953806|qid=Q953806|lt=Bus Stop}} and walk for about 10 minutes.
** {{ill|JR Gifu Station Bus Terminal|Q11226229|qid=Q11226229}} Platform 13 "Suwayama Danchi" "{{ill|Gifu Prefectural Kakamihara Senior High School|Q11471490|qid=Q11471490|lt=Kakamigahara High School}}" "{{ill|Techno Plaza|Q11319203|qid=Q11319203|lt=Techno Plaza}}" and "{{ill|Mikakino Station|Q6845663|qid=Q6845663}}".
** {{ill|Meitetsu Gifu Bus Stop|Q11415771|qid=Q11415771}} Take the bus bound for ``Suwayama Danchi,'' ``Kakamigahara High School,'' ``Techno Plaza,'' and ``Mikakino Station'' at bus stop 6.
* {{ill|Kakamigahara City Fureai Bus|Q11412316|qid=Q11412316}}
** Get off at Sohara Line "Sohara Furuichibacho" bus stop and walk for about 8 minutes.
